untested: Pagination: no limit/offset/page parameters are implemented. Requests with limit/offset were sent and observed to be ignored; there is no contract to assert beyond that.
Authentication/authorization: no auth mechanism exists. Every request was sent without an Authorization header and succeeded; protected-role flows cannot be exercised.
Persistence across restarts: repositories are in-memory only, so no database-backed durability, transactions or concurrent-write behaviour can be tested.
Duplicate project key uniqueness: no uniqueness rule is documented or enforced; no pass/fail expectation can be defined.
Due-date semantic validation: only the JSON type is checked. ISO date-format validation is not implemented and was not asserted.
Concurrency/race conditions on task numbering: all requests were sent sequentially.

bugs.title: Project create/update endpoints have no runtime request validation
bugs.explanation: No global ValidationPipe is registered and the project DTOs are TypeScript-only interfaces, so they vanish at runtime. POST /projects accepts an empty body, missing key/name, arrays, wrong field types, unknown fields and read-only fields. PATCH /projects/:id accepts read-only fields and wrong types, and the repository stores them verbatim.

bugs.title: Missing projects return HTTP 200 with an empty body instead of 404
bugs.explanation: fetchOne() and updateProject() return null for a missing/foreign project and the controller returns that value directly. Nest serialises null as 200 with Content-Length: 0. Task endpoints correctly throw NotFoundException, so this is inconsistent.

bugs.title: PATCH /projects/:id allows mass assignment of internal nextTaskNumber
bugs.explanation: ProjectPatch publicly includes nextTaskNumber and the repository applies any supplied value. A client can set the task counter (e.g. to 50), and the next task key becomes KEY-50 instead of continuing the sequence. Internal server-managed state must not be client-writable.

bugs.title: Invalid and empty project PATCH requests mutate updatedAt
bugs.explanation: update() unconditionally writes a fresh updatedAt even when the patch is empty or all values are unchanged. Task PATCH correctly implements a no-op check and preserves updatedAt.

bugs.title: Invalid project status filter is silently treated as "no matches"
bugs.explanation: The status query parameter is passed straight to the repository as a ProjectStatus with no validation. An invalid value such as INVALID or active returns 200 [] instead of 400. Task filters are validated.

bugs.title: Unknown task query filters are silently ignored
bugs.explanation: TasksService.validateFilters() rejects unknown fields, but the controller only forwards status, priority and assigneeId via individual @Query decorators. An unknown query parameter never reaches the service, so ?foo=bar returns 200 instead of 400. The service-level validation is unreachable over HTTP.

bugs.title: Swagger documentation omits request bodies and mislabels optional query params
bugs.explanation: /docs-json contains no requestBody schemas for POST/PATCH operations. Query parameters derived from @Query("name") are marked required: true even though they are optional in code. This is a documentation defect, not a runtime failure.

bugs.title: Partial task PATCH overwrites unspecified fields with undefined
bugs.explanation: TasksService.updateTask() builds a patch containing every optional key, using undefined for fields the client did not send. InMemoryTasksRepository.update() spreads that patch over the stored task, so undefined replaces existing values and JSON.stringify omits them. A PATCH that only changes title silently wipes status, priority, description, assigneeId and dueDate.
